tldr_label: TL;DR — Wall Street has its worst day since June as Intel craters; Iran weighs Vance's letter; Likud cries foul

tldr_bullets.label: Markets
tldr_bullets.body: The S&P 500 fell 1.8% and the Nasdaq about 2.9% on Friday after Intel dropped 29%, its worst day since the 1970s. October ended with a third straight losing week. [[TAG:danger:S&P -1.8%]]

tldr_bullets.label: Iran
tldr_bullets.body: Tehran confirmed it received Vance's letter but has not replied, and Qatari mediators returned to Tehran. Hegseth fired the Pentagon's top military planner over alleged leaks.

tldr_bullets.label: Israel
tldr_bullets.body: Likud says the election was 'stolen'. Police found no basis for the broad claim, and the Shin Bet is running a 'limited' probe into suspected foreign funding. [[TAG:warning:claims unproven]]

tldr_bullets.label: Ukraine
tldr_bullets.body: The US approved a $2.1 billion sale of Patriot missiles, but Zelensky warns deliveries could take years. Evacuations from Oleshky began under the local ceasefire.

tldr_bullets.label: EU-Canada
tldr_bullets.body: The Montreal summit committed to an 'ever-closer association' but dropped the 'associate member' label Carney had promoted.

tldr_bullets.label: US vote
tldr_bullets.body: More than 49 million Americans have voted early, above the 2022 total, heading into the final weekend before Tuesday's midterms. [[TAG:info:vote Nov 3]]

sections.title: Tech Rout
sections.summary: Intel's 29% collapse caps a brutal October as doubts grow over AI spending

paragraphs.heading: Friday's close
paragraphs.body: The Washington Times, carrying AP, reported that Wall Street had its worst day since June. The S&P 500 fell 1.8% for a third straight losing week, the Dow lost 572 points to 51,770.31, and the Nasdaq fell 747.73 points to 25,437.00. Yahoo Finance said October ended with a 'brutal sell-off', and StockTitan said Nvidia was among the heaviest drags. [[TAG:danger:Nasdaq -2.9%]]

paragraphs.heading: Intel
paragraphs.body: CNBC reported that Intel had its worst day since the 1970s, wiping about $12 billion off the US government's stake. GuruFocus put the drop at 29% after a third-quarter miss. Yahoo Finance said the company's weak outlook and slowing PC demand drove the fall. TheStreet said Reddit also fell after its earnings report.

paragraphs.heading: Oil
paragraphs.body: Trading Economics said Brent climbed above $112 on Friday, near four-year highs, on fears that US strikes on Iran could resume. Investing.com put the close at about $113.57. Settlement figures differ across data providers, partly because the December contract expired. [[TAG:warning:figures vary]]

sections.title: Iran Waits
sections.summary: Tehran confirms it got Vance's letter but has not replied; Qatar's mediators return

paragraphs.heading: No reply yet
paragraphs.body: i24NEWS reported that Iran confirmed receiving Vance's letter seeking renewed talks but has not responded. The Washington Times reported that Qatari diplomats returned to Tehran on Friday for more talks. Dawn said Trump's description of the letter as being about medical supplies conflicts with US media reports that it aimed to restart negotiations. Iran says the US must first meet its conditions on Hormuz, frozen assets, sanctions and troop withdrawals. [[TAG:warning:accounts differ]]

paragraphs.heading: Pentagon shake-up
paragraphs.body: The Washington Post and PBS reported that Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth fired the Pentagon's top military planner even as Trump weighs new strikes on Iran. Al Jazeera said the Pentagon accuses Lt. Gen. Brett Sylvia of leaking classified information to the media. CBS News reported that lawyers say the Pentagon's disclosure of his failed polygraph tests may have violated privacy law. He has not been charged.

sections.title: Israel's Contested Count
sections.summary: Likud alleges a 'stolen' election; Shin Bet calls its foreign-funding probe 'limited'

paragraphs.heading: Fraud claims
paragraphs.body: CNBC reported that Israel faces weeks of coalition bargaining as Netanyahu's Likud claims the election was 'stolen'. Axios described the claim as an attempt to delegitimize the results. Likud has offered testimonies to authorities but no public proof, and police said there was no intelligence support for its broader allegations. Eisenkot called the claims a coordinated campaign. [[TAG:warning:no evidence shown]]

paragraphs.heading: Interference probe
paragraphs.body: The Jerusalem Post reported that the Shin Bet is investigating suspected Qatari and Turkish funding to raise Arab turnout, and it warned against blaming Arab voters. Haaretz said Mossad will assist. Middle East Eye, citing Shin Bet sources, said the probe is limited and will not affect the results. Qatar denies interfering. ABC News (Australia) reported that the elections committee chief requested the investigation.

paragraphs.heading: Next steps
paragraphs.body: NPR said Herzog's consultations will follow certification of the results. Arab News outlined Eisenkot's options, including a minority government supported from outside the coalition.

sections.title: Ukraine
sections.summary: US approves $2.1 billion Patriot sale; Oleshky evacuations begin as Dnipro goes dark

paragraphs.heading: Patriots
paragraphs.body: NBC News and Bloomberg reported that the US approved a $2.1 billion sale of 500 Patriot interceptors to Ukraine after shipment delays. The purchase is funded by Canada, Germany, Norway and EU-backed loans, not US money. CBS News and the Kyiv Post reported that Zelensky warned deliveries could take years. [[TAG:info:500 interceptors]]

paragraphs.heading: Front lines
paragraphs.body: ABC News (Australia) reported that an aid convoy reached Russian-held Oleshky and evacuations began under the local ceasefire. CNBC reported that Russian strikes plunged Dnipro into a blackout, and Zelensky warned of more missile attacks.

sections.title: Europe and Canada
sections.summary: Summit pledges an 'ever-closer association' with no associate label; French yields near 5%

paragraphs.heading: Montreal outcome
paragraphs.body: The EU Council published a joint statement from the summit. The Globe and Mail reported that Canada and the EU committed to an 'ever-closer association' covering the economy, technology and security, and that the statement does not call Canada an associate member. Time said Carney set a target for Canada to become the EU's first 'associate' member anyway, and that the relationship is to be defined by 2027. The two sides will open talks on Canadian access to the EU's Galileo and IRIS2 satellite systems.

paragraphs.heading: French debt
paragraphs.body: Bloomberg's rates page showed France's 10-year yield near 4.97%. CNBC has reported that France is flashing euro-crisis warning signs, although analysts say the region's safeguards are stronger than in the 2010s. [[TAG:warning:French yields ~5%]]

sections.title: Asia and Africa
sections.summary: Prosecutors again seek death for Yoon; Sudan accuses Ethiopia over drone attacks

paragraphs.heading: South Korea
paragraphs.body: Al Jazeera and SCMP reported that special prosecutors again sought the death penalty for former President Yoon Suk-yeol at his appeal over the 2024 martial law decree. He is currently serving a life sentence. His lawyers said the argument lacked evidence. South Korea has not carried out an execution since 1997.

paragraphs.heading: Sudan and Ethiopia
paragraphs.body: Dabanga and allAfrica reported that Sudan accuses Ethiopia of allowing 162 drone attacks to be launched from its territory. Sudanese officials say the attacks killed more than 400 civilians. The claims have not been independently verified, and Ethiopia has previously rejected allegations that it supports the RSF. [[TAG:warning:unverified]]

sections.title: US Midterms
sections.summary: Record early vote tops 49 million as the campaign for Congress enters its final weekend

paragraphs.heading: Final weekend
paragraphs.body: Reuters, via Yahoo, reported that more than 49 million Americans have already voted, according to the University of Florida's Election Lab, compared with nearly 46 million before Election Day in 2022. Reuters said Trump will campaign in Florida, Iowa and Kansas after first canceling the Iowa and Kansas rallies. Al Jazeera said Democrats lead national polling averages, but not every Senate race. PBS NewsHour reported the surge in early voting. [[TAG:info:49M early votes]]
